visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 correctly shows the projectile arc, axes, launch angle, and velocity components in the appropriate locations, while Lesson 2 mostly shows a Desmos setup with undefined/missing theta and no visible trajectory or correctly scaled range diagram.

interactivity.rationale: Lesson 1 includes a well-formed fill-in gate wired after act_introduction with a real prompt, answer, hint, success message, and remediation path, while Lesson 2 has no available gate specs or plan and therefore provides no functioning checkpoint.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 1 has clear, natural narration with no raw LaTeX or garbling despite a minor unit/phrasing slip, whereas Lesson 2 has no transcript/narration available at all, making it substantially worse on audio narration quality.

sync.rationale: Lesson 1 at least provides several cues that generally occur near the narrated references, despite notable missing cues for equations and symbolic steps, whereas Lesson 2 has no transcript or timing data at all, making synchronization effectively absent and worse.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 correctly decomposes velocity, uses vertical motion to find flight time, and applies constant horizontal velocity to get the correct range, while Lesson 2 has no available transcript or lesson content to establish any conceptual accuracy or pedagogical explanation.

polish.rationale: Lesson 1 has a cleaner, consistent full-frame presentation with legible centered title text, while Lesson 2 is visually cluttered by browser chrome, chat widgets, controls, and off-center/overlaid elements despite its larger text.

aggregator.explanation: All six dimension agents strongly preferred Lesson 1, with high confidence across visual accuracy, interactivity, narration quality, synchronization, concept accuracy, and polish. Lesson 1 was credited with correct projectile visuals, functioning interactive checkpoints, clear narration, usable timing cues, sound physics explanation, and cleaner presentation. Lesson 2 was consistently penalized for missing or unavailable lesson content, no narration/timing/gate specs, weak or absent trajectory visualization, and cluttered presentation. The unanimous high-confidence verdict makes Lesson 1 the clear overall winner.
